claim: Characteristics of materials are formally called properties.
Rulers are used to measure lines and record values in centimeters.
A balance scale can be used to compare the mass of everyday objects like an eraser and a sharpener.
Qualitative properties include descriptive terms like small or made of wood.
Malleability is the property that allows materials to be formed into flat, thin objects.
Chemical properties are observed when materials are exposed to environmental factors.
Objects in the environment can be categorized into living things and inert (non-living) things.
Living things are distinguished by having a combination of qualities, including growth, movement, reproduction, and feeding, while non-living things may have some but not all of these qualities.
Seed germination involves observable changes in size, shape, and position over several days.
Living bodies perceive and respond to phenomena occurring both internally and in the surrounding environment.
The energy of an object upon impact affects the amount of water displaced.
Changing liquid water into a gas (water vapor) requires a specific action (adding heat).
Everyday objects like televisions, radios, and mobile phones are common examples of devices students interact with that need energy.
Materials that allow electricity to pass through are called conductors, and the human body is an example of one.
Energy can be transformed from one type to another, such as the energy invested in pedaling converting into mechanical energy.
Objects can be classified by whether they allow light to pass through or block it to form shadows.
Light can be decomposed into various colors.
Inkjet printers use the combination of subtractive colors to produce images of different colors.
Colors are necessary for signage, for example, green and white for emergency signs and red with white for stop signs.
Earth rotates on an imaginary axis passing from pole to pole.
Earth's rotation on its axis every 24 hours causes day and night.
Earth rotates West to East, causing the Sun to appear in the East in the morning and West in the evening.
Different parts of the Earth experience different times of day simultaneously due to rotation.
Earth revolves around the Sun, completing one orbit in approximately 365 days.
A leap year occurs every 4 years because Earth's orbit takes 365 days, 5 hours, and 49 minutes.
In El Salvador, the four seasons are not felt with the same intensity; instead, the dry and rainy seasons are perceptible.
Intense rain in vulnerable areas can cause natural disasters like floods and landslides.
Students can identify and point out the parts of a plant.
Plants absorb water and minerals through their roots.
Plants produce oxygen when making their own food.
Plants are used to satisfy human needs.
Fungi are heterotrophs that obtain food by absorption, often by decomposing matter.
Fungi have utility for humanity but can also cause diseases.
Some animal body parts are adapted to allow them to move.
Animals are grouped into herbivores, carnivores, and omnivores based on their diet.
Wild animals should not be kept as pets.
It is important for humanity to protect animals.
Indirect measurement of circumference can be done using string and a ruler.
A balance compares an unknown mass with known masses until equilibrium is reached.
Folding paper into a fan shape changes its structural resistance.
Electrical current flowing through a conductor can increase its temperature.
Elastic potential energy is stored when an elastic body is deformed by force.
Domestic animals are those accustomed to living with humans.
Hollow tubes placed inside a container can serve as a shelter structure for insects.
Insect shelters should be placed in quiet areas because insects are disturbed by human traffic.
A terrarium is a miniature garden that can house plants and decorative elements.
Accidents can happen anywhere and at any time.
Risk is defined as the probability of suffering harmful consequences.
It is crucial for students to know what to do in an emergency.
Water running through soil with plant cover comes out clear.
Non-biodegradable waste usually comes from human-made products.
Not washing hands after using the bathroom is a cause of illness.
Vaccines create defenses in the body.
Some foods require preparation and cannot be eaten raw.
Handwashing removes invisible organisms that cause diseases.
Everyday products have specific units for volume and mass.
Centimeters are the standard unit for length measurements in these activities.
Large scales cannot accurately measure very small masses like a spoonful of salt.
A reliable instrument is one that functions correctly and can be trusted for accurate measurements.
Thermometers are used to measure temperature in medical and everyday contexts.
Forces are required not only to start movement but also to stop it.
Friction is a force that opposes motion.
The amount of force required to move an object is proportional to its mass.
Iron filings can be sprinkled over a magnet to observe its effects.
The text introduces gravity as the intuitive downward pull from our planet.
Equilibrium can involve rotational forces known as torque.
Projectile motion involves moving both up/down and forward/backward.
Matter undergoes modifications that are classified into physical and chemical changes.
Irreversible changes occur when matter cannot return to its initial state.
Substances are simple if made of one type of particle, and compound if made of different particles.
Mixtures can be classified into homogeneous and heterogeneous categories.
Separation methods are chosen based on the specific properties of the mixture's components.
Rocks are divided into three large groups according to their origin: igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic.
External and internal processes form and transform rocks, constituting the rock cycle.
The shape of a volcano is determined by the composition of the magma.
The Earth's interior is divided into compositional layers including the mantle and the core.
The air contains oxygen, which is essential for maintaining life on the planet.
The hydrosphere includes various bodies of water such as lakes, rivers, and seas.
97% of Earth's water is salt water and 3% is fresh water.
Increased rainfall results in rivers carrying more water.
Infiltration is the process of water penetrating soil layers to reach an aquifer.
Droughts negatively affect living beings and ecosystems.
Water follows a cycle of extraction from the environment, human use, and return.
Substances that dissolve in water are soluble, and those that do not are insoluble.
A more intense color in a solution indicates a higher concentration of the dissolved substance.
Solutions have invisible dissolved particles, while colloids have larger particles visible against the light.
Decantation involves pouring the supernatant liquid into another container without disturbing the sediment.
Filtration can be performed by placing cotton over a strainer to cover all spaces.
Water cleaning can involve sequential steps like filtration through rocks and sand.
Plants are divided into the shoot system above ground and the root system below ground.
Stems and roots function to transport water and food, and to support the plant.
Transpiration is the process by which plants lose water and cool themselves.
After pollination, the fruit forms to house and transport seeds.
Plants are divided into seedless plants (like ferns and mosses) and seed plants.
Tropisms are slow responses plants use to move toward or away from a stimulus.
Gravitropism is the plant's response to the stimulus of gravity.
Seismonasty is a plant's response to relatively strong tactile stimuli.
Tropisms are slow responses in the direction of the stimulus.
The textbook states that some animals have radial symmetry around a central axis.
Mosquitoes develop through distinct stages, starting with eggs turning into larvae.
Taxisms are directional movements either toward (positive) or away from (negative) a stimulus.
Animals have specific anatomical structures adapted for their unique feeding methods.
The textbook states that the concentration of dissolved oxygen is higher in air than in water.
Vertebrates are characterized by having an internal skeleton with a backbone.
Mollusks are characterized by soft bodies and sometimes protective shells.
Sponges are simple animals full of holes for water circulation.
Cnidarians have a hollow sac shape with surrounding tentacles.
Annelid worms have elongated bodies with segments or rings.
Arthropods possess a hard outer covering.
Vertebrate groups can be distinguished by their skin coverings, such as scales for reptiles and hair for mammals.
A dichotomous key involves choosing between two options at each step to identify an organism.
The textbook states that not all tetrapods, such as sea turtles, whales, and seals, currently live on land.
Cells are classified as prokaryotic if they lack a nucleus and eukaryotic if they have one.
Viruses are not considered living because they lack cells, metabolism, and the ability to reproduce independently, which are traits associated with living things.
Viruses lack cells, lack metabolism, and can only reproduce using other living beings.
Pathogens can have protective covers, such as cell walls and capsules.
Detergents can disassemble the protective covers of pathogens, eliminating both bacteria and viruses.
Common household substances can be identified and tested for their efficacy in purifying water against microorganisms.
Fungi develop from spores when food is available.
Protozoa can live in stagnant water and hunt other microorganisms.
Microorganisms require optimal conditions like moisture and adequate temperatures to survive.
Dehydration involves removing water from food, which can be done by adding salt.
Refrigeration and freezing lower the temperature of food to prevent the proliferation of microorganisms.
Microorganisms in fermented food control pathogens by creating a toxic environment for themselves and other microorganisms.
Encurtido is a technique where foods are submerged in salt or vinegar to preserve them.
Drying fish is a method observed locally that prevents decomposition.
Simple machines are classified into six specific groups.
Second-class levers have the resistance located between the fulcrum and the power (effort).
The human body uses joints as fulcrums, such as the tips of the toes when moving ankles.
To apply less effort, the distance between the fulcrum and the effort must be increased.
Complex machines are composed of two or more simple machines connected together.
Hard technology consists of tangible products that can be seen and touched.
Energy undergoes transformations when used by household appliances.
Energy consumption is calculated by multiplying the appliance's power by the hours it is used.
The total cost is obtained by multiplying the energy consumption by the local price per kWh.
Electronic devices consume energy even when turned off, so they should be disconnected to save energy.
Foods are composed of different materials called nutrients.
Foods provide specific amounts of kilocalories that can be recorded and calculated.
Higher caloric intake requires more physical activity to expend the energy.
Accurate anthropometric measurement requires removing items that interfere with height or mass.
BMI is calculated by dividing mass in kg by height in meters squared.
Cultivating plants involves specific sequential activities like soil preparation, sowing, and care.
A supply chain involves multiple activities and distribution methods to bring a product to the consumer.
Products from further away have more steps in their supply chain.
Graphical representation helps visualize study results easily.
Raw foods must be separated from cooked foods.
Ecosystems contain biotic and abiotic components.
Energy enters the ecosystem through producers.
A habitat is defined as the physical place where an organism lives.
Ecological interactions include predation, competition, mutualism, commensalism, and parasitism.
The absence of an organism in a food chain prompts analysis of systemic consequences.
Rainfall amount is determined by reading the water mark on a scale.
Geological phenomena are categorized into internal and external types.
The interaction of baking soda and vinegar produces a chemical reaction.
Threats in El Salvador can be classified as natural or anthropogenic.
A risk map identifies community zones that could be affected by hazards.
The Sun's energy is generated in its core.
Earth's rotation causes the day and night cycle.
Earth's axis of rotation is tilted at 23 degrees.
Nutation is the periodic oscillation of Earth's axis of rotation.
The most accepted hypothesis for the Moon's formation is a giant impact.
Moon phases depend on the Moon's orbital position relative to Earth.
A lunar eclipse occurs when Earth is between the Sun and the Moon.
The heliocentric model places the Sun at the center.
Scale models can be used to represent astronomical distances.
The solar system contains rocky planets and gas giants.
Asteroids are rocky bodies smaller than planets but larger than meteoroids.
Meteorites are meteoroids that reach the Earth's surface.
Artificial satellites are distinct from natural satellites like the Moon.
Voyager probes are the most distant human-made objects in the universe.
The mouth is the initial organ of the digestive system where mechanical digestion begins.
Mechanical digestion by teeth reduces food size to facilitate chemical digestion by saliva.
Respiration involves taking in oxygen and eliminating carbon dioxide.
Lungs expand and contract to move air, which can be modeled using balloons.
Arteries transport blood from the heart to the body's organs.
Kidneys are responsible for removing waste products from the blood.
Physical exercise increases vital capacity because the body demands more oxygen.
The heart pumps blood to all body organs, a process that adapts to physical demands.
The circulatory system transports nutrients, oxygen, carbon dioxide, and waste throughout the body.
Urine characteristics are determined by the waste substances produced by the body's use of nutrients.
The skeleton is a set of bones providing a firm structure and protection.
The skeleton protects vital organs like the brain, heart, and lungs.
Joints are classified by their range of motion into immobile, semi-mobile, and mobile.
Muscles attach to bones and pull them to allow movement.
The five senses correspond to the ears, nose, eyes, tongue, and skin.
The nervous system relates functions and stimuli of different body parts.
The brain includes the frontal, parietal, occipital, and temporal lobes, and the cerebellum.
Neurons capture information from sense organs and send it to the brain.
We respond to stimuli through the joint action of the nervous and musculoskeletal systems.
The female reproductive system consists of the vagina, uterus, fallopian tubes, and ovaries.
The male reproductive system includes testes, epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicles, prostate, urethra, and penis.
Male and female reproductive systems have distinct organs.
Fertilization occurs in the oviducts.
Menstruation is the shedding of the endometrium from the uterus.
Puberty consists of bodily changes produced mainly by sex hormones.
It is important to list and practice care for the reproductive system.
The SI system defines seven fundamental measurable properties of nature.
SI symbols are written in lowercase letters unless derived from a proper name.
Direct measurements are taken for various physical quantities using specific instruments.
Derived magnitudes are created by combining two or more fundamental magnitudes.
Conversions are necessary when dealing with measurements in different units.
If the first discarded digit is greater than 5, the preceding digit is increased by one.
Scientific notation uses base 10 powers to express very large or very small quantities.
Precision and accuracy are two distinct and important characteristics of measuring instruments.
Measurement errors are classified into personal, instrumental, and environmental categories.
Calculating the area involves multiplying measurements, which also requires calculating the propagation of their errors.
Distance is a scalar quantity.
Locations on a map can be found using geographic coordinates.
MRU is characterized by covering equal distances in equal times.
MCU requires a circular trajectory.
An object remains in its state of motion if the net force is zero.
Torque measures the effectiveness of a force in causing rotation.
Elastic potential energy is associated with the force of a spring.
Gravitational potential energy depends on the object's height before descending.
Kinetic energy is associated with the motion of an object before impact.
Mechanical energy is conserved in a closed system during transformations.
Many scientists throughout history have investigated the composition of matter, leading to different atomic models.
The atom has a central, dense nucleus.
Neutrons are calculated by subtracting protons from the mass number.
Modifying the number of neutrons in an atom introduces the concept of isotopes.
Relative atomic mass is the sum of the isotopic contributions.
Losing electrons results in a positively charged ion called a cation.
Objects with the same electrical charge repel each other.
The principal quantum number determines the energy level.
Electrons fill lower energy orbitals first according to the Aufbau principle.
Electrons are placed one by one in each orbital with upward spin first.
Electron configurations indicate how electrons are ordered, revealing how many an element can yield or accept to form bonds.
Döbereiner's triads were an early attempt to systematize chemical elements.
The textbook asks students to determine the number of protons, electrons, and neutrons for an atom given its atomic number.
Columns in the periodic table are called groups.
Group 1 elements, excluding hydrogen, are classified as alkali metals.
An element's electron configuration determines its location on the periodic table.
The textbook asks students to identify how atomic radius increases in a group and period.
A chemical formula indicates the composition of a substance.
An atom that loses electrons is a cation, and one that gains electrons is an anion.
The ionic radius of cations and anions differs from their neutral atoms.
The textbook asks students to identify the oxidation numbers for specific representative groups.
When the cation and anion have the same oxidation number, the subscripts are simplified and not written.
The expansion of the universe is evidence of the Big Bang theory.
Redshift is a phenomenon involving the change in wavelength.
Planets formed through the accretion of matter.
A nebula is an interstellar cloud of dust and gas where stars are born.
A star's evolutionary phases depend on its mass.
The outer core is composed of liquid iron and nickel.
The terrestrial model explains the formation of the Earth's crust.
Earth's magnetosphere absorbs energy from the solar wind.
A space station is an artificial construction designed for activities in outer space.
Satellites require a container to hold and protect their instruments.
Relative dating determines the sequential order of events without providing an exact age.
Fossilization involves the death of an organism, followed by burial in sedimentary materials which compact to form rocks that preserve the fossil.
An extinction is defined as the total or partial disappearance of species in a specific period.
Convergent boundaries occur when tectonic plates collide and one is introduced or subducts beneath the other.
Intensity refers to surface effects, while magnitude refers to the amount of energy released.
Seismic activity is a key parameter monitored to detect changes in volcanoes.
Soil is divided into distinct layers called horizons, each with specific physical and chemical characteristics.
Soil texture is a critical physical property that determines functions like the percentage of voids.
Vegetation protects soil from erosion by acting as a stabilizing reinforcement.
Land use capacity is classified based on the soil's natural aptitude for specific types of production.
Density is a specific property for each substance that relates mass and volume.
The buoyant force is equivalent to the weight of the displaced fluid.
Submerging an object displaces a quantity of water related to its volume.
Pressure increases when the contact surface area decreases.
Hydrostatic pressure depends on density, gravity, and depth (referred to as height in the formula).
Pressure on an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally in all directions.
Surface tension is related to cohesive forces.
Flow rate is expressed as volume over time.
The textbook prompts an investigation into the relationship between pipe section and flow characteristics.
Increasing the speed of a fluid decreases its pressure, though the text's application to drones contradicts this.
The textbook states that high fluid speed over a propeller generates high pressure below it, allowing ascent.
Temperature is related to the movement of atoms and molecules.
Clouds form through the condensation of water vapor and the sublimation of ice crystals.
Lower atmospheric pressure causes water to boil at temperatures below 100 °C.
An increase in temperature leads to an increase in gas pressure inside a container.
Heat and thermal energy are measured in Joules.
Heat is transferred through three mechanisms: conduction, convection, and radiation.
A higher heat capacity means more heat is required to change the substance's temperature.
The human body eventually adapts by reaching thermal equilibrium with the ambient temperature.
To measure battery voltage, the multimeter is set to DC voltage and probes are placed on the respective terminals.
To measure current, the circuit must be opened and the multimeter connected in series.
The color code is used to calculate the theoretical resistance value.
Disconnecting a component in a series circuit stops the current flow through all components.
Components in a parallel circuit share the same voltage as the power source.

Magnetic field lines exit the north pole and enter the south pole.
Ferromagnetic materials are attracted because their internal magnetic domains align with the external magnetic field.
An electromagnet is built by coiling wire around a core and stripping the ends for electrical connection.

Valence electrons are those found in the outermost energy level of an atom.
Atoms seek to have eight electrons in their valence shell to achieve stability.
Covalent bonds involve the sharing of electron pairs between atoms.

Physical changes alter appearance but not the essential chemical composition of matter.
In a chemical equation, reactants are on the left and products are on the right, separated by an arrow.
A neutralization reaction occurs between an acid and a base.
Reactions that absorb heat from their surroundings are called endothermic.
Carbohydrates are also known as sugars.
The reactants that enzymes work on are called substrates.
Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells have fundamental characteristics that can be investigated and compared.
Tissues represent a specific level of biological organization.
Plastids, such as chloroplasts, have a double membrane.
Biologically useful energy drives cellular work.
There are specific mechanisms that exemplify passive transport.
Cells swell when placed in a hypotonic medium.
Mitochondria are necessary for aerobic cellular respiration.
Plants produce sugars through the process of photosynthesis.
The Golgi apparatus is a structural component of the cell.

In prokaryotes, DNA is located in the nucleoid region.

External fertilization occurs outside the mother's body, typically in an aquatic environment.

Vertebrate embryonic development can be represented using models or simulations.
